ci(release): publish componentized .capsule (was raw wasm) (#25)

The release workflow published a raw `cargo build` wasm — a core module
the kernel cannot load. `astrid capsule install` expects a `.capsule`
archive (component + manifest + bundled WIT), so it fell back to
clone-and-build (needs a Rust toolchain) and **binary-only / Homebrew
installs failed**.

Now componentizes via `astrid-build` (fetched from the public astrid
release) and publishes `dist/*.capsule`.

Validated end-to-end: released `astrid-build` → `.capsule` → `astrid
capsule install` (binary-only, no cargo) → tools reach the LLM.

chore(deps): bump astrid-sdk to 0.7.1 (#24)

Bumps the locked astrid-sdk from 0.7.0 to the published 0.7.1.

0.7.1 carries the `tool_describe` macro fix (the describe-fan-out
responder now publishes its descriptor instead of returning it —
capsules built on 0.7.0 answered the tool-describe fan-out with
nothing), plus the additive astrid:process persistent tier and
capabilities::enumerate.

Lock-only — the `astrid-sdk = "0.7"` pin already allows 0.7.1. Required
because the release build is `--locked`, so without this the shipped
capsule stays on 0.7.0. Part of the coordinated fleet bump to 0.7.1.

chore(manifest): correct Capsule.toml version 0.2.0 → 0.1.0 (#23)

## Summary

`Capsule.toml` has carried a stray `version = "0.2.0"` since the early
self-contained-identity commit (#4, March 2026), while `Cargo.toml` and
the only release tag (`v0.1.0`) are both `0.1.0`. No `0.2.0` was ever
tagged or released — the manifest version simply drifted ahead and was
never reconciled.

This realigns the manifest to the actual released version so the capsule
reports a single, consistent `0.1.x` version (and nothing in the fleet
claims `> 0.1`).

## Changes

- `Capsule.toml`: `version = "0.2.0"` → `"0.1.0"` (manifest-only;
matches `Cargo.toml` and tag `v0.1.0`)

chore: commit Cargo.lock and enforce --locked builds (#22)

Commit the resolved `Cargo.lock` (`"0.7.0"`) and add `--locked` to
CI/release builds.

Capsules are deployable `cdylib` WASM end-artifacts (`publish = false`),
not registry libraries, so the lock should be committed: it pins the
exact `astrid-sdk` an artifact is built against and makes builds
reproducible. Previously the lock was gitignored and CI ran without
`--locked`, so every build re-resolved from scratch. `--locked` now
makes a stale/drifting lock fail the build instead of silently shipping
a mismatched SDK.

Build hygiene; no behavior change. Part of a fleet-wide rollout.

chore: scrub stale wasi-target references (#21)

## Summary

Cleanup follow-up to the per-domain WIT migration. README + release
workflow still pointed at `wasm32-wasip1` / `wasm32-wasip2`, but the
canonical Astrid guest target is `wasm32-unknown-unknown` (zero
`wasi:*` imports). Cargo config + rust-toolchain.toml were already
pinned correctly during the migration; this scrubs the last two
holdouts that would have broken release-tag builds and misdirected
new contributors copy-pasting from the README.

## Test plan

- [x] `grep -rE 'wasm32-wasip[12]'` returns zero hits in this repo
- [x] release.yml `cargo build` step compiles for
      `wasm32-unknown-unknown` (same target as CI)

feat!: migrate to per-domain WIT + wasm32-unknown-unknown (#20)

## Summary

Migrate this capsule to:

1. The per-domain WIT host ABI introduced in `unicity-astrid/astrid#752`
(paired with `unicity-astrid/sdk-rust#44`).
2. `wasm32-unknown-unknown` as the canonical build target — zero
`wasi:*` imports, every host call routed through audited `astrid:*`
interfaces.

## Changes

- `.cargo/config.toml` — `target = "wasm32-unknown-unknown"` with
`--cfg=getrandom_backend="custom"` rustflag so `getrandom 0.4` picks up
the SDK's `__getrandom_v03_custom` extern (routes entropy through
`astrid:sys/host.random-bytes`).
- `rust-toolchain.toml` — `targets = ["wasm32-unknown-unknown"]`.
- `[patch.crates-io]` — points `astrid-sdk*` / `astrid-sys` /
`astrid-types` at the in-tree workspaces so the polyrepo cross-cuts
resolve.
- Call-site updates for the new typed-`error-code` SDK surface where
touched.

## Pairs with

- `unicity-astrid/astrid#752` — kernel-side migration
- `unicity-astrid/sdk-rust#44` — SDK migration
- All other `unicity-astrid/capsule-*` PRs on `feat/per-domain-wit`

## Test Plan

- [x] `cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --release` clean
- [x] `cargo clippy --release -- -D warnings` clean
- [x] Loads + runs under the migrated kernel — verified end-to-end via
`astrid run "say hi"`

chore(deps): bump astrid-sdk to 0.6.1 (#19)

Bumps `astrid-sdk` dependency from 0.6.0 to 0.6.1.

Picks up:
- `ipc::publish_as` / `ipc::publish_json_as` (uplink principal
propagation, sdk-rust #37)
- Canonical-WIT-sourced contracts with per-interface `pub mod <iface>`
namespacing (sdk-rust #39)
- `cargo publish -p astrid-sys` fix (sdk-rust #36)

No source change required — `astrid-sdk` 0.6.1 is API-compatible at
every site this capsule touches.

chore(manifest): convert to Cargo-like [publish]/[subscribe] schema with canonical wit refs (#18)

## Summary

Converts `Capsule.toml` to the new Cargo-like manifest schema (RFC:
cargo-like-manifest in the rfcs repo, parser support in
`unicity-astrid/astrid#713`):

* Move legacy `[capabilities].ipc_publish` / `ipc_subscribe` arrays into
typed `[publish]` and `[subscribe]` tables.
* Replace `"TODO"` wit refs on resolvable topics with the canonical
`@unicity-astrid/wit/<noun>/<record>` path.
* Drop remaining TODOs onto newly-added canonical WIT refs where
applicable.

Other capabilities (sandboxing, fs/net allowlists) preserved verbatim.
No src changes — manifest-only, behaviour unchanged.

## Dependencies

* RFC: `unicity-astrid/rfcs#26` (cargo-like manifest schema).
* Parser: `unicity-astrid/astrid#713` (cargo-like manifest schema parser
in core). The kernel reads both legacy and new forms equivalently during
the migration window.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo build --target wasm32-wasip1 --release`
- [x] Capsule loads cleanly under a daemon running the
cargo-like-manifest parser PR.

fix: auto-detect existing spark.toml on first build request (#13)

## Summary

- When KV state says `onboarded=false` but `home://.config/spark.toml`
exists on disk, auto-load the config and set `onboarded=true`
- Guards against empty stubs (requires non-empty `callsign`)
- Makes the system resilient to KV resets

## Dependencies

Requires SDK 0.5.3+ (`fs::read_to_string` status prefix from
unicity-astrid/sdk-rust#25) to avoid WASM traps on file-not-found.

## Test plan

- [x] Spark persona "Nova" loaded from spark.toml on persistent daemon
- [x] Onboarding prompt shown when no spark.toml exists
- [x] Verified via `--snapshot-tui` in smoke test #604

Part of unicity-astrid/astrid#604

Bumps `astrid-sdk` to 0.5.2 which fixes `tool_describe` `FnResult`

fix: store spark.toml in home:// not cwd:// (#11)

## Summary

spark.toml is the LLM's persistent identity — it belongs in
`home://spark.toml` (principal home), not the project CWD. It should
follow the user across all projects.

Also removes `cwd_dir` env entirely — identity has no project-scoped
files.

Part of unicity-astrid/astrid#601.

## Changes

- `src/lib.rs`: spark path changed to `home://spark.toml`
- `Capsule.toml`: capabilities changed to `fs_read/write = ["home://"]`,
`[env]` removed

## Test Plan

- [x] Builds cleanly against `wasm32-wasip1`
- [ ] `/identity-export` writes to
`~/.astrid/home/{principal}/spark.toml`
- [ ] `/identity-import` reads from same path

refactor: rename workspace:// VFS scheme to cwd:// (#10)

## Summary

Renames `workspace://` VFS scheme to `cwd://` across this capsule
(companion to core rename PR).

`workspace://` implied a structured project workspace concept, but the
scheme simply maps to the daemon's CWD at boot. `cwd://` is accurate,
generic, and immediately understood.

Find-and-replace only — no behaviour change.

## Test plan

- [ ] Capsule builds cleanly against updated kernel
- [ ] Smoke test passes

SDK 0.5.0 rewires `#[astrid::tool]` to generate IPC interceptor arms
instead of the removed `astrid_tool_call` export. Non-tool capsules are
unaffected functionally — this is a straight version bump.

## Changes

## Test Plan

feat: rename identity.v1 topics to spark.v1 (#8)

## Summary

Rename IPC topics from `identity.v1.*` to `spark.v1.*` to align with the
`astrid:spark` WIT interface name.

## Changes

- `identity.v1.request.build` → `spark.v1.request.build` in Capsule.toml
and src/lib.rs
- `identity.v1.response.ready` → `spark.v1.response.ready` in
Capsule.toml and src/lib.rs

### Re: topic string constants

Gemini suggests extracting hardcoded topic strings to constants. Valid
idea, but this is a cross-capsule concern — every capsule has hardcoded
topic strings. Extracting constants in one capsule without the others
creates inconsistency. Tracked as a follow-up when the SDK provides
generated constants from WIT definitions.

## Checklist

- [x] Capsule.toml topics updated
- [x] Source code topic strings updated

ci: add WASM release pipeline (#5)

Adds a release workflow that triggers on tag push (`v*`). Builds the
release WASM binary (`wasm32-wasip1`) and creates a GitHub release with
the `.wasm` file as a release asset.

This enables `astrid init` to download pre-built binaries instead of
building from source.

## Changes

- New `.github/workflows/release.yml` — tag-triggered WASM build and
release

feat: self-contained identity with KV state, onboarding, and import/export (#4)

## Summary

- Moves spark config from explicit `kv::get/set` calls to struct fields
on `IdentityBuilder`, backed by the `#[capsule]` macro's stateful KV
dispatch (`&mut self`)
- Adds `onboarded: bool` flag — on first boot the system prompt includes
a natural onboarding instruction asking the agent to introduce itself
and derive an identity from the conversation
- Skips the identity preamble until onboarding is complete so the model
has no pre-anchored name before the user interacts
- Adds `/identity-export` and `/identity-import` commands for persisting
spark config to `.astrid/spark.toml`
- Adds `set_identity` tool for the LLM to save the configured identity

## Test plan

- [x] Fresh install: confirm onboarding prompt fires and agent
introduces itself without a pre-set name
- [x] Call `set_identity` with config and confirm subsequent sessions
use the configured identity
- [x] Run `/identity-export` and confirm `.astrid/spark.toml` is written
- [x] Run `/identity-import` and confirm identity is loaded from file

+**The identity and system prompt builder for [Astrid OS](https://github.com/unicity-astrid/astrid).**
 
-In the OS model, this capsule is `/etc/profile`. It reads workspace configuration and assembles the agent's identity, environment context, and tool usage guidelines into a system prompt.
+In the OS model, this capsule is `/etc/profile`. It owns the agent's spark identity, persists it as capsule state, and assembles the identity plus environment context into a system prompt.
 
 ## How it works
 
-On an `identity.v1.request.build` event:
+On a `spark.v1.request.build` event:
 
-1. Reads the spark identity from `spark.toml` (callsign, class, aura, signal, core directives) or falls back to a default "You are Astrid" preamble
-2. Adds environment context (working directory, platform)
-3. Appends tool usage guidelines (file operations, search, execution, general principles)
-4. Reads project instructions from `AGENTS.md` (or `ASTRID.md` as fallback)
-5. Reads workspace bounds from `.astridignore`
-6. Publishes the assembled prompt on `identity.v1.response.ready`
+1. Loads the persisted spark identity from capsule KV state.
+2. Auto-detects `home://.config/spark.toml` if KV state is empty.
+3. Adds environment context (working directory, platform).
+4. Publishes the assembled prompt on `spark.v1.response.ready`.
 
-Stateless. Reads workspace files fresh on every request. Session ID is echoed back for react loop correlation.
+If no identity exists yet, the prompt includes onboarding instructions. After onboarding, the LLM calls `save_identity`, which saves the chosen callsign, class, aura, signal, and core directives to capsule state and writes `home://.config/spark.toml` as a recovery copy.
+
+State is scoped by Astrid's capsule KV isolation for the calling principal. Session ID is echoed back for react loop correlation.
 
 ## IPC protocol
 
 | Direction | Topic |
 |---|---|
-| Subscribe | `identity.v1.request.build` |
-| Publish | `identity.v1.response.ready` |
+| Subscribe | `spark.v1.request.build` |
+| Subscribe | `tool.v1.execute.save_identity` |
+| Subscribe | `tool.v1.request.describe` |
+| Subscribe | `cli.v1.command.execute` |
+| Publish | `spark.v1.response.ready` |
+| Publish | `tool.v1.execute.*.result` |
+| Publish | `tool.v1.response.describe.*` |
+| Publish | `agent.v1.response` |
